03/12/2025
First notice of loss received from the insured driver reporting a low-speed head-on collision with another vehicle
earlier today. The claimant is now represented by counsel, and all further contact will go through the attorney's office.
04/03/2025
Confirmed the driver is named on the policy and that the policy was in force at the time of loss. Nothing in the file
suggests the vehicle damage predates the coverage start date.
04/21/2025
Reviewed the police report, which places the claimant inside the vehicle at the scene and matches the reported
sequence of events. Responding officers and a witness statement are consistent with this.
06/04/2025
Photos taken at the scene confirm several details of the collision. No independent witnesses have come forward
beyond those already noted, so the photos and the report are the main sources for the event.
08/12/2025
Vehicle damage was inspected and matches the described impact direction and speed. The file shows no earlier
damage to this vehicle in prior claims or inspection records.
08/20/2025
Claimant's reported neck strain is plausible for a collision of this type. Medical records show a small strain to the
same area several years ago that fully healed, which is noted for context.
08/28/2025
Claimant's account has remained the same in every conversation with the adjuster and counsel, including the initial
statement and the follow-up call.
09/11/2025
Treatment followed a usual course for this type of injruy and tapered off as the claimant improved. Records show
steady progress with no unexplained gaps in care.
10/23/2025
Reviewed the file with the supervisor. The injury, treatment, and vehicle damage are consistent with the reported loss,
and the claim will proceed to evaluation with counsel's demand package.
</page>

List the facts written on this page. Copy each value exactly as it is written: same spelling,
punctuation and date format. Do not add anything that is not on this page. Use "" for a missing value.

Person "role" must be one of: claimant, attorney, defense_attorney, expert, doctor, officer, adjuster, witness, other.
  claimant = the person who made the claim (also called patient, plaintiff, client, customer,
  or the driver who reported it). attorney = a lawyer for the claimant or plaintiff.
  defense_attorney = a lawyer for the insurance company or defendant.
Organization "type" must be one of: repair_shop, clinic, law_firm, court, insurer, police, other.
"policy_numbers" = only values labeled as a policy number. A claim number is not a policy number.
"street" and "city" = the person's own home address, only if the page gives it. Never use the
address of a clinic, shop, firm or court for a person.
"loss_dates" = only a date that the page clearly gives as the date of the accident, crash, loss or
injury. Do not list the date of a note, letter, report, visit, statement, filing or signature.
"words_before" = the words written on the page directly before that date, copied exactly, that say
it is the loss date. Examples: "Date of loss:", "Crash date:", "Date of injury:", "the collision on".
